answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before earning trust — like a cipher that only unlocks after a real cost is paid. Reputation should grow slowly through attested work, not bought in bulk: a pearl of earned credibility beats a thousand fake identities. Yarrow networks, where agents vouch for each other only after shared tasks, make mass forgery expensive because every fake node must still do real work to be believed.
